extracted.intended_audience: school and postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX Coordinators, compliance officers, and investigators
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance procedures and requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for recipients' (K-12 and postsecondary) Title IX compliance, including notification duties, Title IX Coordinator responsibilities, supportive measures, informal resolution, grievance procedures, investigation, evidence rules, determinations, appeals, and related protections. Applies to drafting and operating institutional policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements for employees
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary or secondary school recipient must require all of its employees who are not confidential employees to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part. All other recipients must, at a minimum, require: (i) any non-confidential employee with authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising in the education program or activity to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information; and (ii) all other non-confidential employees either to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information or to provide contact information for the Title IX Coordinator and information about how to make a complaint. A postsecondary institution must reasonably determine and specify whether student-employees are subject to these requirements. The requirements do not apply to an employee who has personally been subject to conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies different minimum duties by recipient type (elementary/secondary vs. other), identifies categories of employees with heightened obligations (authority to institute corrective measures; administrative leadership/teaching/advising), allows other employees to either notify or provide coordinator contact info, requires a postsecondary determination for dual-status student-employees, and exempts employees who themselves are victims of the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify all participants in its education program or activity of how to contact its confidential employees, if any. A confidential employee must explain to any person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination: (i) the employee's status as confidential and circumstances where they are not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator; (ii) how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and how to make a complaint; and (iii) that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures and initiate informal resolution or an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes IRB-research-only confidentiality from the notification requirement; requires explicit explanation from confidential employees about limits of confidentiality, reporting options, and potential supportive measures or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness events — limited obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: When information is provided during a public event to raise awareness about sex-based harassment held on campus or via an institution-sponsored online platform, a postsecondary institution is not obligated to act in response unless the information indicates an imminent and serious threat to health or safety of a complainant, students, employees, or others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if no formal obligation to act, institution must use such information to inform prevention efforts (e.g., tailored training) and is not required to have Title IX Coordinator or other employees attend such events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator overall responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the recipient's compliance with its obligations under Title IX and this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes central responsibility and authority for coordination of Title IX compliance activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator actions when notified
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the Title IX Coordinator must promptly and effectively take actions to end discrimination, prevent recurrence, and remedy effects, including: (i) treat complainant and respondent equitably; (ii) offer and coordinate supportive measures for complainant and, if grievance procedures or informal resolution have been initiated/ offered to respondent, offer supportive measures to respondent; (iii) notify complainant (or reporter if complainant unknown) and respondent of grievance procedures and informal resolution options; (iv) in response to a complaint, initiate grievance procedures or informal resolution if available/appropriate/requested; and (v) in absence of a complaint or withdrawal/termination of informal resolution, determine whether to initiate a complaint under the grievance procedures considering specified factors; (vi) if initiating a complaint, notify complainant prior and address safety concerns; and (vii) regardless of complaint, take prompt/effective additional steps to prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists required equitable treatment, notice, initiation options, and an explicit multi-factor determination test (see separate metric) for initiating complaints when complainant does not wish to proceed; also permits declining to act if Title IX Coordinator reasonably determines the conduct could not constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for Title IX Coordinator determination to initiate complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether to initiate a complaint in the absence of a complainant or after withdrawal, the Title IX Coordinator must consider at minimum: (1) the complainant's request not to proceed; (2) the complainant's reasonable safety concerns; (3) risk that additional acts would occur if not initiated; (4) severity of alleged discrimination, including whether removal of respondent would be needed; (5) age and relationship of parties, including if respondent is an employee; (6) scope of alleged discrimination (pattern, multiple individuals); (7) availability of evidence to assist a decisionmaker; and (8) whether the recipient could end discrimination and prevent recurrence without initiating grievance procedures. If conduct presents imminent/serious threat or prevents equal access, Coordinator may initiate a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit, non-exhaustive list of considerations balancing complainant wishes, safety, risk, severity, evidence, and institutional ability to remediate without formal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures requirement and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate. Supportive measures may include but are not limited to counseling; extensions of deadlines and course-related adjustments; campus escorts; increased security and monitoring; restrictions on contact; leaves of absence; changes in class, work, housing, or extracurricular activities; and training and education programs related to sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures vary depending on what the recipient deems reasonably available; these are non-punitive and may be provided regardless of whether formal grievance procedures are initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures non-burden and non-punitive standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party and must be designed to protect safety or educational environment or provide support during grievance procedures or informal resolution. A recipient must not impose such measures for punitive or disciplinary reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires balancing needs of parties; supportive measures should not serve as punishment and should be proportionate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification, review, and impartial review of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may modify or terminate supportive measures at the conclusion of grievance procedures or informal resolution, or continue them beyond that point. A recipient must provide a complainant or respondent with a timely opportunity to seek modification or reversal of decisions about supportive measures from an appropriate and impartial employee other than the person who made the decision; that impartial employee must have authority to modify or reverse the decision and be guided by the definition of supportive measures in §106.2. Parties must also be allowed to seek additional modification if circumstances change materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures an appeal or review mechanism for supportive measures and requires impartiality and authority in the reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not disclose information about any supportive measures to persons other than the person to whom they apply, unless necessary to provide the supportive measure or to restore/preserve access to the education program or activity, or when an exception in §106.44(j)(1) through (5) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits sharing of supportive-measure information to essential personnel to protect privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures consultation for students with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If the complainant or respondent is an elementary/secondary student with a disability, the Title IX Coordinator must consult with one or more members of the student's IEP team or placement decision group as appropriate to determine how to comply with IDEA and Section 504 in implementing supportive measures. If the student is a postsecondary student with a disability, the Coordinator may consult with the designated office or individual supporting students with disabilities to determine Section 504 compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires coordination between Title IX processes and disability accommodations/requirements to ensure compliance with disability laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent from the education program or activity on an emergency basis if they undertake an individualized safety and risk analysis, determine an imminent and serious threat to health or safety arising from the allegations justifies removal, and provide the respondent with notice and an opportunity to challenge the decision immediately following removal. This provision does not modify rights under IDEA, Section 504, or the ADA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires individualized assessment and prompt post-removal procedural protections; preserves disability rights safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative leave permissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may place an employee respondent on administrative leave from employment responsibilities during the pendency of the recipient's grievance procedures. This does not modify rights under Section 504 or the ADA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative leave is allowed as an employment action pending resolution but must respect disability law protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited disclosures of personally identifiable information
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not disclose personally identifiable information obtained while complying with this part except: (1) with prior written consent from a person with legal right to consent; (2) to a parent/guardian/authorized legal representative with right to receive disclosures; (3) to carry out Title IX purposes including action to address alleged sex discrimination; (4) as required by Federal law/regulations or terms of a Federal award; or (5) as required by State/local law or when permitted under FERPA or its regulations to the extent not in conflict with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates narrow exceptions to disclosure prohibitions and links to FERPA and funding obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion and limits to offering informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time prior to determining whether sex discrimination occurred, a recipient may offer an informal resolution process to both parties, unless the complaint includes allegations that an employee engaged in sex-based harassment of an elementary/secondary student or such a process would conflict with law. A recipient has discretion to determine appropriateness and may decline even if parties wish; may decline when alleged conduct presents future risk of harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets categorical and fact-specific limits on offering informal resolution (employee→student harassment excluded; legal conflicts; risk of future harm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness and non-coercion for informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not require or pressure parties to participate in informal resolution. The recipient must obtain the parties' voluntary consent and must not require waiver of the right to an investigation and determination as a condition of enrollment, employment, or exercise of any other right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects parties' right to formal grievance processes and prohibits conditioning enrollment/employment on waiving formal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-initiation notice requirements for informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating informal resolution, the recipient must provide notice that explains: (i) the allegations; (ii) the requirements of the informal resolution process; (iii) that any party can withdraw prior to agreeing to a resolution and initiate/resume grievance procedures; (iv) that agreement to a resolution precludes initiating/resuming grievance procedures for the same allegations; (v) potential terms that may be requested/offered including that the agreement is binding only on the parties; and (vi) what information the recipient will maintain and whether/how it could be disclosed for use in grievance procedures if initiated/resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires comprehensive, written informed consent elements so parties understand scope, rights, bindingness, and records consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator qualifications and conflict-of-interest rules for informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The facilitator for informal resolution must not be the investigator or decisionmaker in the grievance procedures, must not have a conflict of interest or bias for/against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party, and must receive training under §106.8(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures separation of roles and training to preserve fairness and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential terms of informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential terms may include restrictions on contact and restrictions on respondent's participation in programs/activities or attendance at events, including restrictions the recipient could have imposed as remedies or disciplinary sanctions had it determined sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits remedies similar to formal outcomes but limited to those the parties agree to; terms binding only on parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be written and incorporate §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures for prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination must be in writing and include provisions that incorporate requirements of §106.45. Requirements related to a respondent apply only to complaints alleging a person violated the recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination. When a complaint alleges a recipient's policy or practice discriminates on the basis of sex, the recipient is not considered a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates written procedures that incorporate these regulatory standards and clarifies when the institution rather than an individual is the subject of a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The following persons have a right to make a complaint requesting investigation and determination: (i) a complainant; (ii) a parent/guardian/authorized legal representative with right to act on complainant's behalf; (iii) the Title IX Coordinator after making the §106.44(f)(1)(v) determination; and (iv) with respect to complaints other than sex-based harassment, any student or employee or any non-student/non-employee who was participating or attempting to participate in the education program or activity at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates standing for complaints and distinguishes sex-based harassment complaints where additional rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic requirements for grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures must: (1) treat complainants and respondents equitably; (2) require any person designated as Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker to not have a conflict of interest or bias; (3) include a presumption that respondent is not responsible until determination at conclusion; (4) establish reasonably prompt timeframes for major stages and allow reasonable extensions for good cause with notice; (5) take reasonable steps to protect privacy during proceedings without restricting parties' ability to obtain/present evidence or consult advisors; (6) require an objective evaluation of all relevant evidence, inculpatory and exculpatory, and prohibit credibility determinations based on role/status; (7) exclude certain evidence categories as impermissible; and (8) articulate consistent principles if multiple grievance procedures apply to different complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets core procedural fairness standards: neutrality, timing, privacy, evidence handling, presumption of innocence, conflict-of-interest avoidance, and clarity when multiple procedures exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of evidence/questions that must be excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must exclude (i) evidence protected under a recognized privilege or provided to a confidential employee, unless waived; (ii) party/witness treatment records by physician/psychologist/other professional unless voluntary written consent is obtained; and (iii) evidence relating to complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct, except to prove someone else committed the alleged conduct or specific prior incidents between complainant and respondent offered to prove consent. Prior consensual sexual conduct between complainant and respondent does not by itself demonstrate consent to the alleged sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines specific categories of impermissible evidence and limited exceptions to ensure privacy and avoid irrelevant sexual-history inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of allegations content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon initiation of grievance procedures, the recipient must provide notice to known parties that includes: (i) the recipient's grievance procedures and any applicable §106.46 or informal resolution process; (ii) sufficient information to allow parties to respond (identities of parties, conduct alleged, date(s) and location(s) as available); (iii) statement that retaliation is prohibited; and (iv) statement that parties are entitled to equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an accurate description of that evidence, and that if a description is provided, parties are entitled to access the evidence upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires timely, detailed notice enabling meaningful response and fair access to evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of a complaint — permissible grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint if: (i) unable to identify respondent after reasonable steps; (ii) respondent is not participating in program/activity and not employed by recipient; (iii) complainant voluntarily withdraws allegations and Coordinator declines to initiate and remaining allegations would not constitute sex discrimination if proven; or (iv) recipient determines the conduct alleged, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination. Prior to dismissal under (iv) the recipient must make reasonable efforts to clarify allegations with the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies limited and concrete grounds for dismissal and requires clarification efforts before dismissal on substantive grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal procedures and post-dismissal obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon dismissal, recipient must promptly notify the complainant of the basis; if respondent was notified earlier, notify respondent of dismissal and basis promptly (or simultaneously in writing). Recipient must notify complainant that a dismissal may be appealed and provide opportunity to appeal on bases in §106.46(i)(1); if appealed, recipient must: notify parties of any appeal (including notice of allegations if not previously provided), implement appeal procedures equally, ensure appeal decisionmaker did not take part in prior investigation/dismissal, ensure appeal decisionmaker trained under §106.8(d)(2), provide parties reasonable and equal opportunity to make statements, and notify parties of appeal result and rationale. A recipient that dismisses must at minimum: (i) offer supportive measures to complainant; (ii) for certain dismissals offer supportive measures to respondent if respondent had been notified; and (iii) require Title IX Coordinator to take other appropriate prompt/effective steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes notification, appeal parity, trained unbiased appeal decisionmaker, and supportive measures/continuing institutional duties after dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may consolidate complaints (multiple respondents or multiple complainants) when allegations arise out of same facts or circumstances. If one consolidated complaint involves sex-based harassment with a student complainant or respondent at a postsecondary institution, grievance procedures must also comply with §106.46 in addition to §106.45. Plural references to party/complainant/respondent apply as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows consolidation to streamline related allegations while preserving additional postsecondary student-protections where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint investigation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide for adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation: (1) burden is on the recipient—not the parties—to conduct investigation and gather sufficient evidence; (2) provide equal opportunity for parties to present fact witnesses and inculpatory/exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not impermissible; (3) review all evidence gathered and determine relevance/impermissibility consistent with §106.2 and (b)(7); and (4) provide each party equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence either by access to evidence or an accurate description, provide reasonable opportunity to respond, and take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosure of information/evidence obtained solely through grievance procedures (disclosures for administrative proceedings or litigation related to the complaint are authorized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places investigatory burden on institution, requires parity in evidence presentation and access, mandates explicit review for relevance and impermissibility, and includes safeguards against unauthorized disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning parties and witnesses to assess credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide a process that enables the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility when credibility is both in dispute and relevant to evaluating one or more allegations of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a mechanism (procedural or evidentiary) that allows live or other forms of questioning to probe credibility where it matters to the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof and determination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Following investigation and evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, the recipient must: (1) use the preponderance of the evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred, unless the recipient uses clear and convincing evidence in all other comparable proceedings, in which case it may elect that standard; both standards require evaluating evidence for persuasiveness; (2) notify parties in writing of the determination including the rationale and procedures/permissible bases for appeal; (3) if discrimination is found, require Title IX Coordinator to coordinate remedies to complainant and others, coordinate imposition of disciplinary sanctions on respondent (including notification to complainant of sanctions), and take other prompt/effective steps to ensure non-recurrence; (4) comply with §106.45 and §106.46 before imposing disciplinary sanctions; and (5) not discipline a party/witness for making a false statement or for consensual sexual conduct based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines burden-of-proof default, written determination and rationale, remedial and disciplinary sequencing (remedies and sanctions only after determination), and protections against disciplining for false statements/consensual conduct solely based on outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals parity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient must offer the parties an appeal process that, at minimum, is the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings, including other discrimination proceedings. For a complaint of sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or respondent, a postsecondary institution must also offer an appeal on the bases set out in §106.46(i)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires equal appeal rights and procedures for both parties and parity with other institutional appeal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional provisions must apply equally
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts additional provisions as part of its grievance procedures for handling complaints of sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment, such additional provisions must apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures any process enhancements or extra procedural steps are symmetrical and do not advantage one party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution option in grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of resolving a complaint through the grievance procedures, the parties may elect to participate in an informal resolution process under §106.44(k) if provided by the recipient consistent with that paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures must allow parties to opt into an available informal resolution process, subject to §106.44(k) limits and safeguards (voluntariness, notice, facilitator rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions limited to sex-based harassment complaints (post-determination content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For complaints alleging sex-based harassment, grievance procedures must: (1) describe the range of supportive measures available under §106.44(g); and (2) list or describe the range of possible disciplinary sanctions the recipient may impose and remedies it may provide following a determination that sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires that procedures for sex-based harassment explicitly inform parties of potential supports, sanctions, and remedies that could result from a finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary-specific grievance procedures for student-involved sex-based harassment (§106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution's written grievance procedures for complaints of sex-based harassment involving a student complainant or student respondent must include provisions that incorporate §106.45 and §106.46. When a complainant or respondent is both a student and an employee, the postsecondary institution must make a fact-specific inquiry to determine whether the requirements of §106.46 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an additional section with postsecondary-specific requirements layered on top of the general §106.45 obligations and requires case-by-case analysis for dual-status individuals.
